subject: Islamic Studies
framework: Statutory RE entitlement (no National Curriculum programme of study); the school's own Islamic Studies programme
statusNote: There is no National Curriculum programme of study for RE, so this is the school's own programme, taken from its lesson files (content/lessons/islamic-studies, Reception to Year 9) and the Ibn Baz course plan in the school Drive. The gov.uk RE page was opened but says nothing about independent schools. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one.

sources.title: School Drive: 00 | Course Plan & Design Spec, Important Lessons for Every Muslim (8 units, 38 sessions)

purpose: To know Allah, the Prophet and the faith of Islam through creed, worship and character.
To practise worship correctly and live by Islamic manners at home, school and online.
To build the knowledge and skills needed for the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies course.

toKS4: The KS3 programme feeds the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1) sections. Section A (Prophet's life): Y7 Makkan seerah supports 1.1 to 1.4, Y8 Madinah and Badr support 1.4 and 1.8, Y9 Hudaybiyyah, Conquest and Farewell Sermon support 1.7 and 1.9, Y7 and Y9 hadith units support 1.5. Section B (beliefs): Y7 to Y9 aqidah and iman units support 2.1 to 2.6, Y8 sources of law supports 2.7, Y8 to Y9 akhlaq supports 2.8. Section C (living the Muslim life): fiqh of worship, zakah, sawm and Hajj support 3.2 to 3.5. The Ibn Baz supplementary course supports 2.1 (tawhid and shirk), 3.2 (prayer and wudu) and 2.8 (character) but does NOT cover the Prophet's life (1.1 to 1.9) or the early community (2.9). Also not yet covered: Muhammad's role in justice (1.6), Prophet as leader (1.7) in depth, the earlier prophets Musa, Dawud, Isa (2.2), jihad (3.6), festivals (3.7), marriage and family (3.8) and citizenship (3.9).

links.topic: Timelines and source evaluation in the seerah
links.how: History skills (chronology, sources) are applied to seerah events; Islamic Studies supplies the content.

links.topic: Evaluating sources and reading closely (hadith criticism)
links.how: Reading for evidence and reliability in English supports study of how hadith were preserved and graded.
Arabic terms (salah, wudu, iman) are met in both subjects; each reinforces the other.
Surahs recited in Qur'an lessons are explained in Islamic Studies (for example al-Ikhlas for tawhid).
Maths can note that the word algebra comes from al-Khwarizmi's book title (al-jabr); keep the claim modest.
Zakah as a proportion of wealth gives a real context for percentage work.

links.topic: Makkah, Madinah and the Hajj route
links.how: Geography maps the places that the seerah and Hajj units describe.
Science gives accurate knowledge of the natural world that the 'signs of creation' lesson refers to.

links.topic: Honesty, kindness, neighbours and respectful speech
links.how: Akhlaq units give a faith basis for PSHE themes of character and relationships.
Computing e-safety and the adab online lesson address the same habits.
Shared figures such as Ibrahim are met respectfully in other faith contexts.

gaps: The gov.uk page opened says RE is compulsory to age 18 and that faith schools and academies may set their own syllabus; it does not mention independent schools, so that point is unverified.

The Ibn Baz course plan is a masjid course plan in the school Drive; whether the school adopts it as a timetabled part of the programme is unconfirmed. Its allocation across Years 7 to 9 here is a recommendation (Year 7: 15 sessions, Year 8: 12, Year 9: 10 plus the final review session = 38).
Islamic history after the Prophet (the early community) has no unit in the lesson files.
Hadith and ayat are named by title only; no wording or collection reference was added. Exact references need checking by a teacher before use.
Year 6 repeats the Year 2 and Year 4 aqidah and seerah content; check whether the spiral is intended.
